plan.problema: The swing felt lonely because no one wanted to play with her.
plan.svolta: She decided to go for a quick ride around the swing, hoping someone would notice her and want to join the fun.
plan.finale: Suddenly, a little girl ran towards her, excited to jump together!

jump rope.text:
Corda Saltellante was a skipping rope. He lived in Rose Park. He was a bright red skipping rope and he loved to jump more than anything. But today, Corda Saltellante felt very lonely. No one wanted to play with him. The children were running happily, but they didn’t take him into consideration. The other toys sat quietly on the grass, without moving.

Corda Saltellante huddled under a fragrant rose bush. “I just wish someone to jump with,” he thought. “It’s so boring to be here all alone.” He felt sad and a little frustrated. The roses, who listened to him in silence, seemed a little melancholy too.

Suddenly, Corda Saltellante had an idea! He started to jump quickly, creating a cheerful and lively rhythm. “Jump, jump, jump with me!” he shouted, waving his rope fast and hard. He wanted to attract the attention of the flowers in the park.

The tulips began to lean slightly, the roses moved their petals. Then, a sunflower pushed its way through the other plants, following the rhythm of Corda Saltellante. Soon, a red ball and a teddy bear joined in the fun, jumping and dancing together.

Corda Saltellante was so happy! Finally, he wasn't alone. The joy of jumping and seeing the others play filled him with positive energy. All the toys in Rose Park danced happily in the sunshine. Corda Saltellante’s smile grew even wider. The music of his skipping rope had made everyone happier.

plan.problema: The bouncy rope felt lonely because nobody wanted to play with her.
plan.svolta: She decided to create a cheerful and lively rhythm, hoping to attract the attention of the park flowers.
plan.finale: The flowers began to dance to the bouncy rope’s rhythm, and soon other toys joined the fun.

jump rope.text:
Corda Saltellante lay on the playground ground. It was a colorful jump rope, a bright red with white stars. But Corda Saltellante felt sad. No one was taking her anymore. The other toys – the stuffed animals, the cars, the blocks – ran and laughed by themselves.

“I wish I could play,” sighed Corda Saltellante. “But no one gives me a turn. I’m all alone.”

A little teddy bear, Bruno, came up to Corda Saltellante. “Don’t worry,” said Bruno with his soft voice. “Maybe if you try to do something fun, someone will want to play with you.”

Corda Saltellante thought for a while. Then she had an idea! She focused and started jumping up and down, throwing the rope to the stuffed animals, the cars, and the blocks. “Take it! Try to make it spin!” shouted Corda Saltellante.

At first, some of the toys were scared. Then, a remote control car took the rope with its hook. A stuffed animal took it between its paws. Even the blocks stepped aside and tried to make it spin with their shapes.

Suddenly, the playground was filled with laughter and movement. All the toys were jumping together, creating a colorful circle. Corda Saltellante was happy! She didn’t feel alone anymore. She had lots of friends to play with.

Corda Saltellante continued to jump, throwing the rope to everyone who wanted to participate. It was a wonderful joy. Finally, the whole world of the playground was playing together.

plan.problema: The jump rope felt lonely and no one wanted to play with her.
plan.svolta: She decided to create a colorful circle, throwing the rope to all the other toys in the park.
plan.finale: All the toys had fun together and the jump rope didn't feel lonely anymore.
plan.morale: Playing is more fun with friends.

jump rope.text:
Cordy Hopper lay on the lawn of Rose Park. It was a bright red jumping rope. But Cordy Hopper felt sad. No one wanted to play with her. The children walked past, looked at her, but then continued on their way. “I wish someone would throw me and make me jump,” thought Cordy Hopper.

The sun shone on Rose Park, the roses smelled sweet in the air. Cordy Hopper just wanted to be used, to feel the rhythm of jumping. So she made a decision. “I have to do something to get attention!” she shouted with a light sound as she moved a little.

Cordy Hopper ran quickly around the biggest tree in the park. The rope flew in the air, but the children just thought it was a strange and funny rope. “Look at that rope!” exclaimed one of them. “It’s silly!” laughed the others.

Suddenly, a little blue bird landed on the jumping rope. The bird began to flap its wings and jump up and down with the rope. It was so much fun! Soon, a curious rabbit came closer and started jumping with Cordy Hopper. Then a family of squirrels arrived, everyone wanted to try jumping with the rope.

Cordy Hopper was happy. She wasn’t alone anymore. Rose Park was full of laughter and jumps. Everyone was having fun together. Cordy Hopper realized that friendship is born when you share a little bit of joy.

plan.problema: The bouncy cord felt lonely because nobody wanted to play with her.
plan.svolta: It decided to take a quick spin around the biggest tree to get attention, but the children thought it was just a flying rope!
plan.finale: Then, a little bird perched on the cord and started bouncing, and soon other animals joined the fun.

jump rope.text:
Cordy Skip was a jump rope. He lived at the playground. He was a bright, beautiful red color. But Cordy Skip felt sad. No one wanted to play with him. The other toys, the swings and the seesaws, were always surrounded by children. He lay all alone under the shade of the big oak tree.

“I wish someone would take me,” sighed Cordy Skip. “But no one looks at me.” A little dog, a beagle named Pip, came closer and sniffed Cordy Skip. Then, without saying a word, he ran off to play with the other children.

Cordy Skip felt even colder. He decided he had to do something. He closed his eyes and thought. “If no one wants me, then I have to make myself noticed!” He shouted loudly and started to skip. He skipped faster and faster. He tried to make shapes in the air with the rope. He made circles, little stars, and even a little dinosaur!

The children at the playground stopped to watch him. They were curious about the jump rope that was skipping so much fun. One by one, they started to run around Cordy Skip. They laughed and jumped happily, trying to follow the rhythm of the rope.

Cordy Skip finally felt like he was part of the group. He was happy and joyful. The children ran and jumped, and he kept skipping, creating a cheerful rhythm that filled the air with laughter. Creativity had turned loneliness into a party for everyone.

plan.problema: The skipping rope felt lonely because nobody wanted to play with her.
plan.svolta: She decided to create a cheerful rhythm, jumping faster and making funny shapes in the air to attract attention.
plan.finale: The children, fascinated by the rope moving so playfully, began to run around her, laughing and jumping happily.

kite.text:
Dragon of Paper was a special dragon. He was made of colorful paper and had big, beautiful wings. He lived in the Flowery Meadow, a place full of fragrant flowers. But today Dragon of Paper didn’t want to play. He was sitting on the grass, with his wings down, and he looked very sad.

He couldn’t lift himself off the ground! He puffed slowly, but he stayed still. “I wish I could fly!” he exclaimed. “It’s so frustrating!” He felt a little bit guilty because he just wanted to have fun. A little butterfly, named Lila, landed on his tail and looked at him curiously.

Dragon of Paper thought. “I need to do something,” he said to Lila. Then he had an idea! The wind was blowing gently among the flowers of the meadow. It was a light but constant wind. Dragon of Paper decided to use that wind to push himself upwards.

He began to move his wings, following the flow of the air. The wind pushed him slowly, and then faster! Dragon of Paper’s wings lifted higher and higher. With one last effort, he soared high up, dancing in the blue sky.

Lila the butterfly flew around him, happy for his friend. Dragon of Paper smiled. He was finally free! He had learned that even when things seem difficult, you have to keep trying and adapt. The wind had carried him high, towards the sun.

plan.problema: The Paper Dragon couldn't lift himself from the ground, frustrated and sad.
plan.svolta: He decided then to use the wind blowing among the flowers to push himself upwards.
plan.finale: Finally, with one last effort, the Paper Dragon soared into the air, dancing in the blue sky.

kite.text:
Drago Volante was a colorful paper dragon. He lived in the Flowery Meadow, full of yellow marigolds and red roses. He loved the meadow, but he felt lonely. Nobody wanted to use him to play. All the other toys had already been taken, and he remained there, leaning against the lavender bush.

“I wish I could fly,” thought Drago Volante. “I wish I could feel the wind under my wings.” But nobody helped him. He was a dragon who didn’t know how to fly, because nobody threw him.

Then, Drago Volante had an idea. He started to move on his own, flapping his tail with all his might. He tried to create whirlwinds of wind! The wind rose, strong and stormy. Drago Volante was carried away from the meadow. He flew higher and higher, away from the marigolds and the roses. He was scared.

A little bird, a yellow finch, saw the dragon flying away. Carefully, he approached Drago Volante and gently took him in his feet. He brought him back to the Flowery Meadow.

As soon as Drago Volante touched the ground, some colorful butterflies approached. The butterflies danced around him, moving their wings. Drago Volante was no longer alone. He was happy to play with the butterflies and the little bird. He realized that sharing his joy made everything more beautiful.

plan.problema: The Flying Dragon felt lonely because nobody wanted to throw him into the sky.
plan.svolta: He decided to attract attention by creating whirlwinds of wind, but the wind was too strong and carried him away from the meadow.
plan.finale: A little bird arrived to pick him up gently and brought him back to the meadow where a group of butterflies approached to play with him.

kite.text:
Dad Dragon was a special kite. He wasn't made of wood or fabric like the other kites. He *was* a kite, with colorful wings and a strong body. He lived in the Flowery Meadow, a meadow full of yellow daisies and tall sunflowers.

Dad Dragon loved to fly. Every day, when the wind blew strong, he tried to go high, near the blue sky. But he never quite managed it. His wings seemed too slow. He stayed just a few meters from the ground, frustrated.

A blue butterfly, Luna, landed on his tail. “Why are you so sad, Dad Dragon?” asked Luna with a sweet voice. “You need to make your wings move faster!”

Dad Dragon understood. He concentrated. He decided to do something different. He started to move his wings up and down, then sideways, trying to make them spin with the wind. He did a fast circle! The wind lifted him, pushed him up high.

Dad Dragon felt powerful. His wings danced in the sky. Slowly, but surely, the meadow became smaller and smaller beneath him. Finally, Dad Dragon soared high up, smiling at the sun. He was so happy!

The wind gently stroked him.

plan.problema: Dad Dragon can’t fly high in the sky.
plan.svolta: He decided to flap his wings faster, doing a whirl with the wind.
plan.finale: Finally, Dad Dragon soared high, smiling at the sun.

kite.text:
Spazzolone was a cheerful and colorful kite. He lived in the Flowery Meadow, a place full of fragrant flowers and soft grass. Spazzolone loved the wind. The wind made him fly high, drawing circles in the blue sky.

One day, the wind was very strong. Spazzolone enjoyed spinning around, but then, suddenly, a gust of wind carried him away. When Spazzolone opened his eyes, he realized he was on the ground, near the meadow. There was no longer wind pushing him up. He was too sad to fly!

Spazzolone couldn't get up anymore. He was too heavy and his strings were loose. He felt lost and alone in the Flowery Meadow. A little beetle, named Leo, approached Spazzolone and asked him what had happened.

“I need to get back up high!” said Spazzolone with a weak voice. He thought of an idea. “I must reach the biggest sunflower in the meadow! Maybe from up there I can see better where the wind is.”

So, Spazzolone began to climb slowly up the stem of the sunflower. It was tiring, but Spazzolone didn’t give up. Reached the top, he saw the wind blowing far away.

Suddenly, a gentle breeze gently picked him up. The wind slowly lifted him, making him fly back into the blue sky. Spazzolone started spinning around happily, grateful for his perseverance. His colorful shape danced among the clouds.

plan.problema: Brush got lost by the wind and can’t get back up high anymore.
plan.svolta: He decided to climb on a big sunflower for a better view.
plan.finale: The wind gently picked him up, sending him flying back into the blue sky.

kite.text:
Dragon Flyer was a toy dragon, a colorful kite with red and yellow paper wings.
He lived in the Flowery Meadow, a place full of white daisies and tall sunflowers.
Every day Dragon Flyer wanted to fly high, very high, but he couldn’t.
He was sad because he never got above the trees.

“I just want to see the world from above,” sighed Dragon Flyer.
“It’s so frustrating!”

He wiggled on the meadow, spreading and folding his wings with force.
He tried to do everything quickly, but the wind always messed him up.
His wings got mixed up and he kept falling to the ground.

A little blue bird, named Pipì, watched Dragon Flyer.
Pipì was a very wise little bird. “Don’t force things,” chirped Pipì.
“Try to move your wings calmly, as if you were swimming in the air.”

Dragon Flyer listened to Pipì. He calmed down and began to move his wings slowly.
He felt the wind on his paper skin. He understood that he shouldn’t fight against the wind, but dance with it.

With every slow and precise movement, Dragon Flyer went higher and higher.
Finally, he reached the top of the tallest tree in the meadow!
He was happy and carefree. 

“Thank you, Pipì!” exclaimed Dragon Flyer. “Now I know how to fly really.”

The sun set over the Flowery Meadow, painting the sky pink and orange.
Dragon Flyer smiled, knowing that with patience and calmness, even the biggest dreams can come true.

plan.problema: The Flying Dragon couldn't fly high in the sky and felt sad.
plan.svolta: He decided to flap his wings faster, but the wind still ruffled them.
plan.finale: A little bird taught him to feel the wind and move his wings gracefully, allowing him to fly high and happy.

kite.text:
Planea was a colorful glider. He lived in the Flowery Meadow, a place full of yellow marigolds and red roses. Planea loved to be there, watching the bees buzz among the flowers. But that day, something wasn't right. Planea couldn't lift off the ground. He was sad.

“I can never go high,” sobbed Planea, with his light fabric swaying sadly. “I feel so heavy.” A white butterfly, named Stella, landed beside him. “Maybe there needs more wind,” said Stella.

Planea thought. The Flowery Meadow was a beautiful place, but the wind always seemed too light. So, Planea made a decision. He started to run! Running fast, fast, fast towards the tallest tree in the meadow, a large maple with green and shiny leaves. 

Planea tried to reach the wind. He felt the ground beneath him, but he couldn't really lift off. Then, suddenly, a light breeze hit him. It was a little wind, but it was enough! Planea started to sway up and down, dancing among the colorful flowers.

Planea finally felt happy. He was flying high, higher than ever before. The marigolds seemed small beneath him, the red roses shone like gems. Planea realized that with a little effort and courage, even the most difficult dreams can come true. And so, Planea continued to fly, happy with his little success.

plan.problema: The Plane couldn't lift off the ground and felt sad.
plan.svolta: He decided to look for the strongest wind in the meadow, running towards the tallest tree.
plan.finale: Finally, a light breeze lifted him into flight, dancing among the colorful flowers.

kite.text:
Dragon Flyer was a colorful paper dragon. He lived in the Flowery Meadow, a place full of yellow and red flowers. Dragon Flyer loved the meadow because he could wave his wings in the wind. But lately, Dragon Flyer felt very sad. He couldn’t fly high, just like he wanted to do.

Every time he pulled the string, he moved a little, but then he always fell to the ground with a thump. “Oh no!” exclaimed Dragon Flyer. “I just want to lift off and see the meadow from up there!” He felt frustrated because his wings seemed too light.

Then, Dragon Flyer decided to do something different. He explained his wings with more strength, pulling the string quickly. But once again, he fell to the ground. “I can’t do it!” thought Dragon Flyer, lowering his head. 

A little bee, Sugar, came closer and looked at him. “Try to be patient,” said Sugar. “And don’t give up.”

Dragon Flyer listened to the bee and tried again. Suddenly, a ray of sunshine hit his colorful fabric. The sun warmed the paper and Dragon Flyer’s wings gently lifted into the blue sky. Dragon Flyer was flying! He was happy and free. 

Dragon Flyer danced with the wind, seeing the flowery meadow from above. The sun shone brighter and brighter, and the colorful dragon continued to climb. Every little effort made a difference.

plan.problema: The Flying Dragon felt sad because he couldn't fly high.
plan.svolta: He decided to stretch his wings with more strength, but he kept falling to the ground.
plan.finale: A ray of sunshine hit his colorful fabric and gently lifted him into the blue sky.

kite.text:
Kite lived in the Flowery Meadow. He was an old kite made of cloth, colored red and yellow. Kite loved the meadow, with its fragrant flowers and butterflies that fluttered by. But Kite felt very lonely. Every day, the other toys in the meadow had fun together, but no one wanted to fly with him. “They never take me,” thought Kite, “am I too old, perhaps?”

One day, Kite was sitting on a wooden bench, watching the clouds. He felt sad and a little angry. Then he had an idea! He decided to draw funny shapes in the sky with his sail. He drew a big heart, then a smile, and finally a little dinosaur.

Kite continued to move in the wind, creating silly shapes in the blue. A little bird, a robin named Pippo, saw Kite’s shapes and flew closer. Pippo flew around Kite, following his movement. Together, Kite and Pippo created a wonderful show for all the animals in the meadow: rabbits jumping, squirrels running, and even Mrs. Crocodile smiled.

Kite didn’t feel lonely anymore. He had a friend, a little robin, and together they did beautiful things. The sun set over the Flowery Meadow, painting the sky pink and orange. Kite realized that kindness and the ability to offer something special, attract friendship.

plan.problema: The Kite felt lonely because nobody wanted to fly with him.
plan.svolta: He decided to draw funny figures in the sky, hoping to attract someone’s attention.
plan.finale: A little bird joined the Kite’s flight, and together they created a wonderful show for all the animals in the meadow.

kite.text:
Papa Drago was a lovely kite. He lived in the Flowery Meadow, full of colorful flowers and green grass. He was made of shiny red paper and had a long white tail that waved in the air. Papa Drago loved to fly, but he had a little problem. He wanted to fly high, really, really high, like eagles!

Every day, when the sun shone in the Flowery Meadow, Papa Drago prepared to fly. He pulled the string with all his strength, but he couldn't go up high. He stayed just a few meters from the ground, a little disappointed. A small yellow flower, a daisy, watched him with curiosity.

“Maybe,” thought Papa Drago, “I need to flap my wings with more strength!” So he pulled the string even faster. But instead of going up high, he started to spin around himself, faster and faster! He was a little confused and frustrated.

Then, a gentle breeze arrived in the Flowery Meadow. The wind stroked Papa Drago’s wings and gently pushed him upwards. With one last pull on the string, Papa Drago soared high in the blue sky! He smiled happily, seeing the Flowery Meadow becoming smaller and smaller below him.

The wind kept making him fly, and Papa Drago realized that with patience and perseverance, even the biggest dreams can come true. His white tail danced in the air, a beautiful sign of joy in the Flowery Meadow.

plan.problema: Dad Dragon couldn't fly high like he wanted!
plan.svolta: He decided to flap his wings with more strength, but he only spun around himself.
plan.finale: Thanks to the gentle wind, Dad Dragon finally soared high, smiling happily.

kite.text:
Kite was a colorful old banner. He lived in the hayfield. He was made of paper and cloth, and he had strong poles. But Kite felt lonely. No one wanted to fly with him. The children preferred cars or teddy bears. Kite dreamed of dancing in the wind, of feeling the sun on his fabric.

“I wish someone would fly me,” Kite thought every time he saw a plane pass high in the sky. “But no one chooses me.”

One day, Kite made a decision. “I have to do something to get attention,” he said to himself. So, he tried to lift himself as high as possible. He wanted to be seen! But when he was at the highest height, he ended up stuck. His poles were trapped between two big hay bales. He couldn't move.

A little bird, a blackbird named Pippo, was flying above the field. He saw Kite in trouble and came closer. Gently, he used his wings to give the banner a light tap. A tap enough to free Kite!

Kite felt relieved. Thanks to Pippo, he was free to wave in the wind. From that day on, Kite and Pippo became friends. They had fun together in the hayfield, and Kite realized that friendship can be born from a simple kind gesture.

plan.problema: The Kite felt lonely because no one wanted to fly with him.
plan.svolta: He decided to jump as high as possible to get attention, but he ended up stuck between two bales of hay.
plan.finale: A little bird, seeing him in trouble, freed him with a gentle flap of its wings.

marbles.text:
Palle di vetro was a little toy made of glass. He lived in a secret garden full of colorful flowers and tall trees. He was happy there, with his sisters and brothers, all glass balls of different sizes. Sometimes they rolled together, making real races through the tall grass.

One day, Palle di vetro found himself in a difficult situation. One of his friends, the smallest, had ended up under a big stone. She couldn't move! She was stuck and scared. “Help!” cried Palle di vetro, but no one seemed to hear him.

Palle di vetro tried to roll with force against the stone. He tried to push, to slide the stone away. But it only made other balls slide away! None of his friends could help her. The situation had become even more complicated.

Then, Palle di vetro had an idea. He found a thin and very long thread that he had found among the roots of a tree. With great care, he tied the end of the thread to the smallest ball. Then, he began to pull gently. The thread stretched and Palle di vetro pulled patiently.

Finally, the smallest ball was freed! All his friends could return to playing together, happy and relieved. Palle di vetro was happy to have solved the problem. He had learned that sometimes things have to be done with calmness and attention. 

It was lovely to see all his friends running happily in the secret garden.

plan.problema: The smallest ball got stuck under a stone and couldn't get out.
plan.svolta: He tried to roll with force, but it just slid away from the other balls.
plan.finale: Then, he used a thin string to gently pull the ball out, freeing all his friends.

marbles.text:
Little Glass Ball was a small blue glass ball. He lived in a secret garden full of colorful flowers and tall trees. He was part of a group of glass balls, all the same shape and the same color. They enjoyed rolling together, making little races in the soft ground.

One day, Little Glass Ball found himself alone. He had tried to make a curve around a rose bush and, suddenly, he had ended up in a tall meadow, full of green grass and thick. He couldn't see his friends anymore! He was scared and sad.

“Oh no!” thought Little Glass Ball. “I have to go back! But the grass is too high.” He sat down on the wet earth, trying to figure out what to do.

Then he decided to do something new. He decided to roll faster, hoping to pass the tall grass and reach his friends. He rolled with all his might, pushing himself forward with great energy. The grass slowed him down a little, but Little Glass Ball didn't give up.

Suddenly, a gentle breeze blew through the garden. The breeze gently pushed Little Glass Ball towards the group of companions. He saw their bright reflections! They rolled together, happy to see him again. 

Little Glass Ball felt proud. He had shown that even if things seem difficult, with a little determination, you can reach your goals. The breeze had helped him, but it was his will that made him move.

plan.problema: The glass ball was lost in the tall grass and cannot return to its group.
plan.svolta: He decided to roll faster, hoping to pass the tall grass and reach his friends.
plan.finale: Thanks to his determination, a light breeze gently pushed him towards the group of companions.

marbles.text:
Little Glass Ball was a small blue glass sphere. He loved to play in the secret garden. It was a magical place, full of colorful flowers and tall trees. Little Glass Ball loved to roll on the soft grass and slide along the gravel paths.

One day, while he was playing, Little Glass Ball found himself in a difficult situation. He had fallen into a small hole under a big stone. The stone was very heavy and Little Glass Ball couldn’t move. He was stuck! He couldn’t roll away.

Little Glass Ball tried to push the stone with all his strength, but nothing worked. Then, he decided to do something different. He decided to roll against the edge of the stone with all his speed. But when he hit it, only a few small pebbles rolled away. Little Glass Ball felt a little sad and frustrated.

Suddenly, a ray of sunshine hit the big stone. The stone began to shine! It reflected the sunlight in a thousand colors. And as it shone, a small passage appeared next to the stone. Little Glass Ball understood right away: he just had to keep trying.

Little Glass Ball rolled with force towards the passage and he got out! He was free! Now he could go back to playing in the secret garden. The sunlight had done its magic. 

Little Glass Ball stopped for a moment, reflecting on his journey. He realized that even when things seem difficult, you shouldn’t give up. And with a little perseverance, you can always find a solution.

plan.problema: The Little Glass Ball got stuck under a big stone, and couldn't get out.
plan.svolta: She decided to roll with force against the edge of the stone, but only made smaller stones slide.
plan.finale: A ray of sunshine hit the stone, making it shine brightly and revealing a small passage for the Glass Ball.

marbles.text:
Palle di vetro was a little blue glass ball. He loved to run in the countryside yard, rolling on the dirt path and zipping through the tall weeds. It was a fun game, but sometimes a little bit dangerous. One day, while running fast, he lost his balance and rolled down a small hill.



He found himself stuck in a deep hole in the ground. The hole was dark and narrow, and Palle di vetro couldn’t move. It was frustrating! He couldn’t get back on his own. He tried to push with his legs, but nothing. He stayed there, still, feeling small and helpless.



He saw a tall brick wall that marked the yard. He thought, “If I could climb that wall, maybe I could reach the other side of the yard and find a way out.” So, he started to climb, crawling along the rough bricks. It was tiring! Every movement was difficult, but Palle di vetro didn’t give up.



Finally, he almost reached the top of the wall. But when he tried to take a step back, he slipped down with a little thump. Palle di vetro fell to the ground, right near the hole he had fallen from. He was happy! He found himself exactly where he had stopped. He promised himself to be more careful when he ran and not to trust too much speed.



Palle di vetro promised himself to play calmly and carefully, because sometimes, patience is the key to overcoming even the most difficult obstacles.

plan.problema: The glass ball got stuck in a hole in the ground, and couldn't get back out.
plan.svolta: He decided to climb the wall to reach the other side of the yard, hoping to find his way back.
plan.finale: Finally, with a little slip, he fell back down to the ground, right near the hole from which he had fallen, and promised to be more careful.

marbles.text:
Big Marble was a very special marble. He was big and red, made of shiny glass. He lived in the Secret Garden, a place full of tall grass and fragrant flowers. Big Marble loved to roll amongst the leaves, but this time he got lost.

He found himself in the middle of a maze of very tall grass. He couldn’t see his colorful box anymore. Everything around him was gray. Big Marble felt sad and a little scared. He tried to roll to the right, then to the left, but the grass was too high!

Big Marble thought he had to do something different. He focused and made a big decision. He decided to roll with all his strength against the rose bush. He hit it with all his energy. The bush shook and Big Marble got stuck among the thorns. But he kept rolling, even stronger!

Suddenly, a powerful thump made the marble box fall right next to him. It was full of other red marbles like him. Big Marble rolled inside, happy and safe. A little bird was sitting on the box and singing a song. Big Marble was glad to be back home. 

Big Marble understood that you must never give up, even when things seem difficult. Perseverance can lead to wonderful results.

plan.problema: He was lost in the maze of tall grass and couldn’t find his way back to his box.
plan.svolta: He decided to roll with force against a rose bush, hoping to make a gap.
plan.finale: The force of the blow made the marble box fall right beside him, safe and sound.

marbles.text:
Palline was a glass ball, shiny and blue. He loved his secret garden very much. It was a special place, hidden behind the old oak tree in the yard. He only played there with him and a few smooth stones. Sometimes, a little caterpillar would pass by to say hello.

One day, Palline was rolling happily when… *poof!* He found himself trapped between the rocks. They were big and rough, and they had made him fall into a small valley. He couldn't get back anymore. “Oh no!” thought Palline. “I can’t get out! I want to go back to the flowery meadow.”

He was scared. The rocks were cold and hard. There was no one to help him. Palline tried to roll, but the rocks were too slippery. He tried to jump, but he was too heavy.

Then, he noticed a reed next to a stone. It was long and thin. “Maybe… maybe I can use this!” thought Palline. Carefully, Palline pushed the reed against the rocks. Slowly, very slowly, the balls began to move towards the edge of the valley.

Palline kept pushing with the reed, without hurrying. After a while, the balls rolled out! They ran happily towards the flowery meadow, where the sun shone and the colors were beautiful. Palline felt relieved and happy. He had been patient and in the end, he had found his way. Patience can help solve even the most difficult problems.

plan.problema: The balls were lost between the rocks and couldn’t find its home.
plan.svolta: He decided to use a straw to gently push the balls towards the edge.
plan.finale: Finally, the balls rolled out, running happily towards the flowered meadow.

marbles.text:
Palle di Vetro was a little blue glass ball. He lived in the yard, right where the sunshine shone the brightest. Palle di Vetro loved to roll, zoom, and take little bounces on the bumpy ground. He was the favorite toy of the yard.

One day, while he was having fun rolling quickly, something bad happened. Palle di Vetro got stuck! One of his arms, the smallest and roundest part, was trapped between the cracks of the old stone wall. It was a forgotten corner of the yard, full of dirt and dry leaves.

Palle di Vetro tried to roll, but he was too heavy to move on his own. He tried to push with all his might, but the wall was rough and crumbly. He couldn’t get free. He felt frustrated and a little sad.

Then, he saw a little crescent moon passing in the sky. It was the wind, blowing gently. Palle di Vetro called out to the wind: “Help me! I’m stuck!” The wind listened carefully. It started to blow with force, but it didn’t help at all.

The wind changed tactics. It blew softly, gently, only on the part of the wall where Palle di Vetro was stuck. The dust and dirt blew away, revealing the cracks. With one last gentle puff, Palle di Vetro slid out, free and happy!

Palle di Vetro rolled happily in the yard, grateful for the help of the wind. He realized that sometimes, even small problems can be solved with a little bit of teamwork.

plan.svolta: He tried to roll and push, but the ball was too heavy and the wall was too rough.
plan.finale: Then he asked for help from the wind, which with a gentle breeze blew away the dust and freed the ball.

Glass Balls was a little glass game. He lived in a basket in the yard. He was always happy to roll and make little slides on the cement. One day, while he was having fun, Glass Balls lost his balance. He rolled too far and ended up in the tall grass. 

It was all green and bumpy! Glass Balls felt very lonely. He looked for his basket, but he couldn't see it. The grass was so big and full of tall grass that it was hard to cross. Every time he tried to roll faster to reach the basket, Glass Balls rolled even further away. It was frustrating!

Suddenly, he heard a voice. “Hello!” It was a little gnome with a red hat and a kind smile. The gnome had a small shovel and helped Glass Balls roll slowly through the tall grass. 

The gnome was patient. He gently pushed Glass Balls with the shovel, without making him go too fast. Together, Glass Balls returned to his basket. The basket was exactly where Glass Balls thought it was! He was happy and glad to be home.

The gnome smiled at Glass Balls. “It was a pleasure to help you,” said the gnome. Glass Balls rolled into the basket, thinking about his adventure and the kind friend who had helped him. 
It was nice to have a friend to help you through difficult times.

Big Marble was a shiny pebble, a bright red like the sunset. He loved to play in the Secret Garden. It was a special place, full of tall grass and colorful flowers. His sandhill was the most beautiful of all. Big Marble loved to roll down it, always fast and happy.

---

One day, while he was having fun zooming across the sand, something bad happened. A big stone, smooth and gray, blocked him. Big Marble was stuck underneath! He couldn’t get back to the top of the hill. It was all dark under the stone and he couldn’t see the sun anymore.

---

Big Marble tried to push with his little sand legs, but nothing. The stone was too heavy. He felt sad and a little scared. A little beetle, Leo, came closer and looked at him worriedly. “Don’t give up!” said Leo.

---

Big Marble took a deep breath. He decided to do something brave. He focused all his strength and rolled hard against the edge of the stone. He heard a thud and the stone began to move! Slowly, very slowly, it moved away.

---

Big Marble ran quickly up. Finally, he reached the top of the sandhill! He was full of joy! He jumped happily and ran back and forth. The sun warmed him and Leo watched him smile. Big Marble understood that even when things seem difficult, with a little courage you can always find a way out.

One day, while they were playing “who can make the most turns,” a ball got stuck! It was the smallest, a red ball, and it had gotten stuck between the roots of a big tree. Palle di vetro tried to push, but she couldn’t move. She was frustrated. “Oh no!” she exclaimed. “I can’t get out!”

Palle di vetro tried to roll, hoping that the tall grass would help. But every time she tried to turn, she got stuck against the wet ground. The red ball was always trapped. Palle di vetro felt very sad.

I’m stuck!” The squirrel, whose name was Noceolino, came closer and looked at the red ball. With his little paws, Noceolino gently pushed the ball. The red ball rolled out of the roots of the tree!

Giradischi lived in the attic. He was a toy shaped like a spinning top, colorful and full of gears and springs. The attic was full of dust and old boxes. Giradischi loved to be there, waiting for the sun to light up the room.

But lately, something wasn't going right. Giradischi couldn't spin as fast as before. He had become very, very slow. He moved with difficulty, almost like a slow-motion movie. “Oh no,” thought Giradischi, “I need to be fast again!”

He tried to push with all his might. He spun around himself, but he was still too slow. He tried to make a big jump, hoping that the spinning would become faster. But he got stuck again! It was frustrating. 

A little rag doll, Lila, watched him with concern. “Maybe,” said Lila, “you need to try to spin even stronger!”

Giradischi thought about it. He focused, he tried hard, and finally, with one last big movement, he felt his spinning become fast and joyful. The wind scattered the dust of the attic as Giradischi spun faster and faster. 

He was happy! Finally, he could do what he loved. Giradischi realized that even when things are difficult, you have to keep trying. And in the end, with a little effort and perseverance, you can reach your goal.

One day, Giratorio noticed something strange. He couldn't spin quickly anymore. He had become very slow. He almost stopped right away! “Oh no!” thought Giratorio. “I can’t do my fast spins anymore!” The dust seemed to have slowed down his movement.

Giratorio tried to concentrate, but it was difficult. He tried to move the little hand that held his body, but nothing. The old clock ticked louder and louder, as if it was laughing at his problem.

Then he had an idea! “Maybe,” he said to himself, “a jump could help!” Giratorio went to an old wooden chest. He looked at it carefully and, with all his strength, jumped onto the chest.

The thump was strong! Giratorio spun faster than ever. After one last whirling spin, he regained his speed. He began to enjoy the memories of the attic, the sound of his movement echoed among the old things. The dust seemed to disappear and Giratorio felt happy again.

“I wish I could make the others happy,” thought Spinny Dance, stopping suddenly. “Maybe if I spun faster…” And he began to spin faster and faster! But every time he tried to make a whole circle, he fell off the wooden table. “Oh no!” exclaimed Spinny Dance, as he found himself upside down next to the yellow flower.

A little teddy bear, Leo, approached him carefully. “Maybe,” said Leo, “you just need to find your own rhythm.” Spinny Dance thought about it. He began to spin slowly, then a little faster, always with care. He felt a little wiggle inside himself and suddenly… it all worked!

His colors became even brighter, shining in the sunshine of the garden. The other toys came closer, curious, and they started to laugh as Spinny Dance spun faster and more gracefully. Spinny Dance realized that perseverance, even when things seem difficult, can lead to happiness. And so, the Flower Garden filled with joy and laughter, thanks to Spinny Dance.

A little kitten, Leo, came closer and meowed. “Don’t worry, Hydro-Sprinkler,” said Leo. “The sun made you too sticky.”

Hydro-Sprinkler thought. “I need to find some shade,” he said. He headed towards the big tree at the playground. The tree was so tall that its shadow made the air cooler. Hydro-Sprinkler collected some leaves wet from the stream near the tree and put them in his tank. The leaves were cool and refreshed the sticky jelly.

After a while, Hydro-Sprinkler felt ready again. He filled the tank with fresh water and went back to the green lawn and started spraying with energy! The water bubbles flew everywhere. Leo watched him happily. 

Hydro-Sprinkler realized that waiting and finding a solution had done good. Patience had made everything perfect again. And while he kept playing, he realized that everything has its own time.

water gun.text:
Ruggine was a bright blue water gun. He lived at the playground, near the slide tower and the red swing. He loved to play with the other toys, but this day was different. He was covered all over with colorful pebbles! Big, small, red, yellow, green… all stuck to his smooth body.

“Oh no!” exclaimed Ruggine. “How did I become so dirty? I feel like I’m drowning!” A boy had shot lots of water jets at him, and the pebbles, attracted by the shiny surface, had stuck everywhere. It was a disaster!

A little seashell, named Leo, came closer to Ruggine. “Maybe you can use your spray to clean yourself,” said Leo. Ruggine thought. He had to do something. He couldn’t just stand there, weighed down by the pebbles.

Ruggine focused. He took a deep breath and then sprayed. A powerful, but gentle, water jet hit the biggest pebbles. They came loose slowly, one at a time. Ruggine continued to spray, with a more precise jet.

With a final, well-aimed spray, Ruggine freed all the pebbles, which returned to shine in the sun. He was clean and shiny again. Leo applauded him. Ruggine felt happy and satisfied. He had learned that even the most difficult things can be solved with patience and perseverance.

One day, the sun was shining brightly in the sky. The sand in the playground had become hot! The children had sat in the shade of the trees, avoiding touching the sand with their hands or feet. Nobody wanted to play anymore; the heat was too strong. Spritz felt a deep sadness. He wanted to see everyone happy and playing.


Spritz moved quickly to the center of the playground. He started to spray a jet of cool water on the hot sand. The water splash was cold and refreshing. A boy, Leo, saw what Spritz was doing and smiled. Other children came closer and started to help Spritz spray water on the sand.


Soon, all the children were running and laughing. They were having fun chasing each other, building sandcastles, and playing with the cool water. Spritz was happy. Seeing the children so happy filled him with joy. The sudden breeze created by the water spray cooled the air of the playground.


Leo came up to Spritz and said, “Thank you, Spritz! You’re the best toy in the world!” Spritz replied, “It was a pleasure to share my water!”

“I have to do something!” said Spritz. So, he aimed his water spray at the first flower. But the water disappeared right away! He tried with another flower, and that water vanished in a moment too. It was hard for the water to evaporate so quickly.

The flowers stayed intact and started to regain their color. The butterflies, seeing the water, approached with enthusiasm and began to fly happily around Spritz.

Spritz was happy. He had learned that even when things seem difficult, you have to be patient and keep trying. After a while, Spritz realized that perseverance can lead to wonderful results.

Suddenly, while he was making a great jump, he found himself stuck at the top of the swing. It was too high to come down.

Yo Yo tried to swing with all his might. He was trying to make him roll down, but the more he tried to move, the higher he went! He started to feel a little scared. He couldn’t do anything. “Help!” he shouted, but nobody seemed to hear him.

Then, a girl and a boy saw Yo Yo stuck. They were sitting on the swing next to it. “Look, he’s having trouble!” said the boy. The girl ran to the sandbox and picked Yo Yo up in her hands. 

“Make some gentle movement,” suggested the girl. Yo Yo followed their advice. Slowly, with small swings, he started to roll down. It was a smooth and safe journey.

Finally, Yo Yo touched the ground! He was happy to be free. The girl and the boy smiled. “Thank you!” said Yo Yo. He realized that asking for help could be the best thing to do. 

Yo Yo started spinning happily again, knowing that friends can help solve problems too.

Armonica Blu wanted to make a melody to make them smile. She tried to press her holes, one at a time. She played “do”, then “re”, then “mi”. But the butterflies didn’t move. It seemed like the right melody didn’t exist.

“Maybe I have to go faster,” thought Armonica Blu. She took a deep breath and played again, but this time the sounds were confused, a strange noise and without rhythm. The butterflies flew away. Armonica Blu was sad.

A little green beetle, Leo, came closer. “Try to play slowly,” said Leo. “And try to hear the sound.”

Armonica Blu listened to Leo. She closed her eyes and thought of a yellow flower she loved so much. Then, calmly, she began to play a simple song. It was sweet and slow. “Do-re-mi-fa-sol,” repeated Armonica Blu.

Suddenly, the butterflies came back. They flew around Armonica Blu, they circled and danced. Their wings shone in the sun. Armonica Blu played the song again, calmly and carefully. It was a beautiful and peaceful melody. 

Armonica Blu understood that sometimes it just takes time to find the right melody. And the secret garden, thanks to its sweetness, filled with a magical atmosphere.

Armonino felt frustrated. He tried to understand what he had done wrong. Then he had an idea. He decided to try something different. He began to press the holes with lots and lots of delicacy. He pressed softly, softly, as if he were stroking the wind.

He slowed down the rhythm. He played small, quiet notes. The daisies listened carefully. Slowly, one daisy moved. Then another, and another still. A little beetle came close to Armonino to watch the music.

The daisies began to dance to the rhythm of his music, happy and bright. Their leaves shimmered as if they were covered in stardust. Armonino played with sweetness, softer and softer, while the daisies twirled in the secret garden. His music was a gift for all the flowers. Screwdriver went up to the robot and started turning the screw that held the arms in place. He turned and turned, but nothing! The screw was too rusty. It was stuck in the metal. Screwdriver tried to turn with more force, but the screw didn’t want to move.

Leo sat down and thought for a little while. Then, Leo found a small bottle of oil for cars. He poured it on the rusty screw. Screwdriver started turning slowly, very slowly. The oil slid away, freeing the screw. With one last gentle turn, the screw moved!

Leo Junior started moving and waving to Leo with his arms. He was happy to be able to play again. Screwdriver was happy to have solved the problem. He had learned that even the hardest jobs become easy with a little patience. And when you have patience, things always go better.

Screwdriver felt frustrated. He tried to turn the screw even harder, but he only damaged it! The head of the screw had become a little dented. “Oh no!” exclaimed Screwdriver. Dr. Bruno, the old carpenter of the workshop, arrived running. “Try to be more gentle,” said Dr. Bruno.

Screwdriver took a deep breath and started to turn the screw very slowly. With small, precise movements, he loosened the screw slightly. Then, with a final gentle tap, he put it back perfectly.

Screwdriver decided to help. He started turning the blocks, trying to make them fit together. But it was difficult! Some pieces didn’t want to stay together. Screwdriver tried with his small tip, but it didn’t work. Then he used his bigger, stronger tip. He tried to push the hardest pieces, but the tower kept falling down.

cacciavite.text:
Screwdriver Leo lived in a wooden workshop full of tools. He was a special screwdriver, red and shiny, always ready for action. The workshop was his world, made of wooden planks, nails, and lots of dust.

One day, he heard a strange noise. It came from the wooden tower, tall and impressive, which he had built himself. Leo ran to check. The screws that held the tower together had come loose! The tower was about to collapse. “Oh no!” thought Screwdriver Leo. He had to do something right away.

Leo started turning the screws with his head, trying to tighten them. He turned and turned, but the screws just spun faster without stopping. It was frustrating! A little hammer, called Pip, came closer. “What’s happening, Leo?” asked Pip.

“The screws don’t want to stay still!” replied Screwdriver Leo. He thought for a moment. Then he had an idea. He took a small clamp from his drawer and used it to firmly grasp the screws. He turned them gently, patiently, and slowly the screws fixed themselves back to the wood. The tower became strong and stable again.

Leo smiled. The tower was saved thanks to his patience. Pip tapped his little feet in approval. Screwdriver Leo realized that sometimes you have to do things calmly, without rushing. 

The wooden tower stood up again, an example of how perseverance can solve even the biggest problems.

Stella was a colorful guitar. She lived in a secret garden full of roses and big trees. Stella loved to play, but she felt very sad. No one seemed to want to listen to her. Her strings vibrated, making beautiful melodies, but no one pressed them to make her play.

“Oh, how I wish someone would listen to me!” sighed Stella, her strings trembling slightly. A little squirrel, Leo, came closer and said, “Stella, maybe it’s because your sound isn’t loud enough.”

Stella thought about it. She realized Leo was right. She decided to do something different. She tucked her fingers under her strings and played as loud as she could. She played with all her energy, hoping the sound would reach even the busy bees and the delicate butterflies that flew in the garden.

She played louder and faster and happier. The sun shone, the flowers smelled sweet. Stella focused on the sound, thinking only about making it go as far as possible. 

Suddenly, a swirl of colors appeared! A group of colorful butterflies, yellow, blue, red, and green, began to dance around Stella. The butterflies followed the rhythm of her guitar. Stella smiled. She was happy! The loud sound had made the difference.

Stella continued to play, and the butterflies danced faster and faster. She realized that you shouldn’t give up when you’re doing something beautiful. 

Persistence can lead to happiness.

plan.finale: The sweet sound of the guitar attracts a group of colorful butterflies that dance around Stella, making her happy.

Nobody seemed to want to listen to him. The garden gnomes were jumping happily, the fireflies were shining, but nobody considered his music. Chitarra Leo strummed softly, hoping someone would appreciate him, but it was just a small sound lost in the green of the garden. He felt like his heart had become heavy.

“It doesn’t matter,” thought Chitarra Leo. “I’ll have a concert for the butterflies!” He decided to play his guitar louder and happier, hoping their flights would be beautiful music to listen to. He sat down under the big tree and began to play a sweet melody.

A little white butterfly landed on his handle. Then more arrived, dozens of colorful butterflies fluttering around Chitarra Leo as he continued to play. The butterflies danced and fluttered following the rhythm of his music. The whole garden filled with colors, with the butterflies shining in the sunlight.

Chitarra Leo smiled for the first time in a long time. His music had brought joy to everyone, even to the butterflies. He realized that true happiness wasn’t just in playing, but in sharing his music with others. And so, Chitarra Leo continued to play, knowing that a shared smile is the most beautiful sound of all.

Stella played on, and the whole garden resonated with joy. She felt surrounded by friends, finally not alone. Her music had brought happiness to all the flowers in the garden.

plan.problema: Stella feels lonely and no one listens when she plays.
plan.svolta: She decided to create a super happy melody, full of bright notes, hoping it would attract the attention of the flowers in the garden.
plan.finale: The tulips and daisies danced to the rhythm of her music, and Stella finally felt happy and surrounded by friends.

chitarra.text:
Stella was a colorful guitar. She lived in a secret garden, full of fragrant flowers and tall trees. Stella loved to play, but she felt very sad. No one seemed to appreciate her music. The flowers didn’t dance, the trees didn’t move, and the sun seemed distracted.

“I just wish someone would listen,” sighed Stella, her strings vibrating softly. “My music is beautiful!”

Stella decided to do something. She focused and began to play louder. She played with all her strength, trying to make her sound bright. The notes resonated in the secret garden, becoming more intense. 

Suddenly, a little squirrel came out of the nearby thicket. It was a friendly brown squirrel with long, fluffy ears. Initially, he was surprised, then his gaze fell on Stella. The little squirrel began to tap his feet to Stella’s music. He tapped on the ground with his tiny paws, following the sound of the guitar.

Stella played even louder and happier. The squirrel continued to tap his feet, creating a fun and cheerful rhythm. It was a strange, but wonderful, symphony. Stella finally felt happy, her music was no longer alone. 

The little squirrel and Stella played together in the secret garden, sharing the joy of music.

plan.problema: Stella felt sad because no one listened to her music.
plan.svolta: She decided to play louder, hoping someone would notice her bright sound.
plan.finale: A little squirrel came out of the woods and began to tap his feet to Stella’s guitar music.

chitarra.text:
Chitarra Stella was a special guitar. She lived in a secret garden full of colorful flowers and tall trees. Chitarra Stella had a shiny wooden body and six strings that shone in the sun. But today, Chitarra Stella felt sad. She couldn't play a happy melody. Her strings were silent and her sound was dull.

“I wish I could play,” sighed Chitarra Stella, “but I don’t know how!” A little squirrel, Nastro, scampered nearby. “What’s wrong, Chitarra Stella?” asked Nastro with his squeaky voice.

Chitarra Stella explained her problem. She tried to tap the strings with a small hammer she had. But the sound was dull and out of tune. It wasn’t a very beautiful melody at all. Chitarra Stella felt even worse.

Then, she remembered something. She remembered how her bird friends sang. With her fingers, she began to move them gently up and down the strings. At first, the sound was uncertain, but then it became clearer and sweeter. A beautiful melody filled the secret garden. The wind whispered along with Chitarra Stella’s music.

Nastro scampered around Chitarra Stella happily. The guitar played such a beautiful song that all the birds in the garden sang together in chorus. Chitarra Stella realized that with a little patience, even the most difficult things can become wonderful. The sun set and Chitarra Stella’s music continued to fill the secret garden.

plan.problema: Stella’s guitar felt lonely and couldn’t play a happy tune.
plan.svolta: She decided to try hitting the strings with a small hammer, but the sound was dull and out of tune.
plan.finale: Then, remembering what her bird friends did, she began to gently move her fingers over the strings and a sweet song filled the garden.

chitarra.text:
Chitarra lived in a flowery meadow. He was a small, red guitar with shiny strings. He loved to play cheerful melodies, but one day something wasn't right. The notes that came out of him were sad and gray. The flowers in the meadow weren't laughing anymore, they had shrunk and seemed faded.

Chitarra tried to move the strings quickly, then slowly. But nothing! He couldn't make music anymore. “Oh no!” thought Chitarra. “What can I do?” He felt very frustrated.

Then he decided to try something strange. He started to beat his body against a big tree in the meadow. He only made strange noises, as if he were trying to speak in an unknown language. None of the flowers got up to listen to him.

Chitarra felt even worse. He closed his eyes and calmed down. He took a deep breath, inhaling fresh air from the meadow. Then, slowly, he began to pluck his strings. A sweet sound filled the flowery meadow! The notes were cheerful again! The flowers got up and started to smile.

Chitarra played his favorite melody, a simple and happy song. He was happy. He realized that sometimes, when things don't go as we want, all you have to do is stop for a moment and try to find calm. Music was full of joy again in the flowery meadow.

plan.problema: The guitar no longer knew how to play cheerful notes and the flowers didn't laugh.
plan.svolta: It decided to try to beat its body against a tree to see if it would unlock, but it only made strange noises.
plan.finale: It calmed down, took a deep breath, and began to pluck the strings slowly, finding the melody it loved.

chitarra.text:
Stella was a colorful guitar. She lived in the yard of the house, under the shade of the big tree. Stella loved to play, but lately she felt very sad. When she tried to make beautiful melodies, no one listened to her. The adults were too busy talking or working in the garden. Even the children rushed past without stopping to listen to her notes.

Stella yawned. “Oh no,” she thought. “It’s so hard to make my music heard.” She huddled on the grass, with the strings slightly muted. She didn’t want to play anything anymore.

Then, Stella had an idea! She decided she would try to make different rhythms. She started to play quickly, with all her strength. She played loud and cheerful, as if she were dancing. The string vibrated and the sound filled the yard.

Stella continued to play, faster and faster. She made fun rhythms with jumps and shivers. Suddenly, she felt a movement behind her. A little black kitten had come closer, curious about the sound. The kitten followed Stella with its tail moving back and forth.

Stella played even louder, happy. The kitten continued to follow her, pleased with her songs. Stella realized that when she really had fun, her music became special. And finally, someone appreciated her melodies. 
Joy is like a song: it’s better to share it with others.

plan.problema: Stella felt sad because no one listened to her melodies.
plan.svolta: She decided to try to make happier rhythms, playing quickly and with a lot of energy.
plan.finale: Finally, someone, a curious kitten, began to follow her with his tail, showing that he appreciated her songs.

elastico per capelli.text:
Elastico Felice lived in the playground. He was a rainbow-colored hair tie and he loved to curl the hair of the dolls. Today, however, he wasn’t happy. He felt loose. He couldn’t hold the hair of a little toy butterfly anymore.

The butterfly was beautiful, with pink and blue fabric wings. It had fallen off its cart and the little girl who had bought it was very sad. Elastico Felice wanted to help her. He tried to pull the butterfly’s hair, but he couldn’t do it. He kept getting looser and looser.

Elastico Felice tried to roll himself faster, hoping that the friction would make him stronger. But it was too smooth! The hair tie slipped away without being able to hold the butterfly’s hair. The little girl sat nearby, thinking.

Suddenly, Elastico Felice had an idea. “Sun!” he shouted. The sun was shining high in the sky and warming the playground. The hair tie went towards the sun and looked at it. The sun sent its warm rays onto the hair tie. It became even smoother!

Elastico Felice rolled the hair tie around the butterfly’s hair. He pulled tight, tight, tight! The hair straightened perfectly. The butterfly was happy again and could go back into its cart. Elastico Felice smiled. He had found the solution with patience.

plan.problema: He loosened it and now can’t hold together a toy butterfly’s hair.
plan.svolta: He tried to roll it faster, but it was too smooth and it slipped away.
plan.finale: He asked the sun for help to polish it, and, becoming smoother, it held the butterfly’s hair perfectly!

elastico per capelli.text:
Elastico Leo was a very lively hair tie. He lived in the playground and loved to roll around in the colorful hair of the children. One day, he found himself in a strange situation. He had disappeared from his favorite spot, a big bright red curl!

Leo felt very sad. He looked everywhere, under the slides and around the sandbox, but the red curl was gone. “Oh no!” thought Elastico Leo. “How will I find my home?”

He decided to do something. He climbed onto the merry-go-round, the tall one with the horses that went round and round. He tried to see from far away, hoping to spot the red curl among so many other hairs. It was a little difficult, because the merry-go-round was moving!

A boy, Marco, was playing near the merry-go-round. He saw Elastico Leo at the top and said, “Look, you’re right here!” Marco pointed with his finger at a red curl of hair, just like the one Leo had lost.

Suddenly, a little ray of sunshine hit Elastico Leo. The ray guided him towards the red curl! Leo unrolled quickly and ended up right in the happy curl of the boy. Everything was okay.

Marco smiled happily. Elastico Leo finally felt safe. Sometimes, patience is the key to finding what we love.

plan.problema: Leo got lost from his colorful hair!
plan.svolta: He decided to climb the carousel to see if he could find his place.
plan.finale: Thanks to a little ray of sunshine, Leo was guided back to the happy hair of the boy.

elastico per capelli.text:
Elastico Leo was a very lively hair tie. He lived at the playground, right next to the swing. He loved watching the children play and chasing after the butterflies. One day, a girl named Sofia sat on the swing. She combed her blonde hair and put Elastico Leo around her head.

Leo was happy! But then, while Sofia laughed and swung, something changed. He started to loosen. Her hair, which was before neat, began to come undone. “Oh no!” thought Leo. “I need to hold Sofia’s hair together!”

Leo rolled himself over and over repeatedly on the sand to tighten himself. He was trying to get stronger and have a better grip. But the sand was too smooth! He couldn't get a hold. He felt frustrated. Sofia, who was watching him, was worried.

“Don’t give up, Leo!” said Sofia. Then, she took some dust from the playground and scattered it around Leo. The dust created little wrinkles in the sand. Elastico Leo rolled himself over again, this time on the dust. And, miraculously, he found a firm grip!

With an effort, Elastico Leo tightened Sofia’s hair firmly. Everything was back in place. Sofia smiled happily. “Thank you, Leo!” she said.

Leo felt proud. He had overcome a small problem thanks to his perseverance. It was nice to help Sofia and make her smile.

plan.problema: Leo loosened and couldn't hold Sofia's hair anymore!
plan.svolta: He rolled over repeatedly on the ground to tighten, but it was too smooth.
plan.finale: Sofia used some dirt to find the right grip and Leo finally tightened her hair firmly.

elastico per capelli.text:
Elastico Leo was a very happy hair tie. He lived at the playground, near the castle tower and the red swing. Every day he saw lots of children playing. Leo loved to watch their laughter.

One afternoon, a little girl named Sofia sat on the swing. Elastico Leo grabbed onto her golden hair to make her a braid. But suddenly, something changed. Leo started to loosen! His strands became looser and he couldn't hold Sofia's hair together anymore.

Sofia started to worry. “Oh no!” she said. “My curls are becoming a mess!” Elastico Leo felt panic. He didn't want to disappoint the little girl. He tried to pull tight, but he was too weak. 

Elastico Leo made a decision. He rolled quickly around a big rock, right there near the sandbox. He felt a little tension, a little new strength! The movement helped him to get stronger. 

After a few turns, Elastico Leo felt much better. Now he could hold Sofia's hair tightly. The little girl smiled, fixing her hair with Leo, who was now stronger and more secure. “Thank you, Leo!” said Sofia.

Elastico Leo felt happy. He had learned an important thing: if you try hard and don’t give up, you can overcome any difficulty. Perseverance always makes everything easier.

plan.problema: Leo loosened his grip and couldn't hold Sofia's hair anymore!
plan.svolta: He decided to roll quickly around a big rock to gain strength.
plan.finale: Sofia smiled, fixing her hair with Leo, who was now stronger and more confident.

elastico per capelli.text:
Elastico Leo was a very active hair tie. He loved to play in the playground. Every day he enjoyed keeping the hair of many children together. But today he had a problem. He had gotten tangled! His strands were woven into a complicated knot and he couldn't anymore straighten the hair of a little stuffed bunny.

The bunny, called Poldo, was complaining: "Oh no, oh no! I can’t play anymore because my hair is messy!" Elastico Leo was trying to pull, to unwind, but the knot was too hard. He felt frustrated and a little sad.

Then he had an idea! He saw a big pinecone that was lying near the sandcastle. He decided to roll around the pinecone quickly. He was spinning around, spinning around, creating spirals. The pinecone helped to loosen the tight strands.

After a little while, Elastico Leo felt much better. His strands were almost free! With one last effort, he managed to untangle the knot completely. The hair of bunny Poldo was smooth and happy again.

Poldo hopped happily: "Thank you, Elastico Leo! You are the best hair tie in the world!" Elastico Leo smiled. He had learned that even difficult things can be solved with calmness and patience. It was a perfect moment to go back to keeping the hair of many children together in the playground.

plan.problema: Leo had tangled himself and couldn't hold a stuffed bunny's hair anymore.
plan.svolta: He decided to quickly wind himself around a pinecone to loosen the knot.
plan.finale: Finally, Leo untangled his threads and the bunny's hair returned smooth and happy.

elastico per capelli.text:
Elastico Leo was a bright yellow hair tie. He lived at the playground, among the swings and the rope bridges. He loved to watch the children play and jump. One day, while wandering among the toys, he found himself tied to a big red swing. It was all thanks to a little gust of wind! Leo couldn't move. He felt frustrated. He couldn't spin around anymore, he couldn't say hello to the rope bridge.

A little girl was playing nearby. Her name was Sofia and she had red hair like the swing. Sofia looked at him with curiosity. “What’s wrong, hair tie?” she asked. “I’m tied up!” replied Leo, a little bit angry.

Elastico Leo realized he had to do something. He closed his eyes and took courage. He started to spin his hair tie quickly around himself. He made it spin, spin, spin! He created friction, a kind of resistance that helped him unwind.

At first it was difficult, but Leo didn't give up. He kept pulling with his hair tie. Finally, with one last effort, he managed to free himself from the red swing. 

Elastico Leo waved goodbye to the swing with a smile. He was happy to be free and ready for new adventures at the playground. He had been brave and he had found his solution.

plan.problema: Leo found himself tied to the swing, unable to move!
plan.svolta: He gathered his courage and started to spin his rubber band quickly to create friction and unwind himself.
plan.finale: Finally free, Leo waved goodbye to the swing with a smile.

elastico per capelli.text:
Elastico Leo was a lively, yellow hair tie. He lived at the playground, among the swings and slides. Every day he helped to keep the braids of a thousand little girls together. He was happy, especially when the wind made him dance.

One afternoon, while holding onto the tail of a little girl, something went wrong. Leo got tangled! He made a huge knot, full of knots and loops. He couldn't get back to his original shape, flat and smooth. It was as if someone had taken away his energy.

Leo tried to relax, but it didn't help. The knot was too strong. A little bird, which was chirping among the trees, watched Leo with curiosity. “It seems difficult!” chirped the bird.

Elastico Leo decided to do something. He started to move quickly, pulling himself up and down. He tried to unwind with force and precision. He strained, he stretched, he shortened. The knot resisted, but Leo didn't give up. He kept moving, faster and faster.

Finally, after many attempts, Elastico Leo lined up perfectly! He was flat and yellow again, ready for another adventure at the playground. The little bird flew away happily.

plan.problema: Leo had gotten tangled and couldn't get back to his original position.
plan.svolta: He decided to make a series of quick movements, trying to unwind with force and precision.
plan.finale: Finally, Leo lined up perfectly, ready for another adventure!

elastico per capelli.text:
Elastic Band Dancer was a very lively hair tie. He loved to play in the playground. Every day he enjoyed making spirals around his friends, the little fluff balls. That day the sun was shining brightly and the air smelled of flowers.

Suddenly, Elastic Band Dancer found himself stuck! He had fallen into a pile of colorful building blocks. He couldn’t move anymore. It was all dark around him. “Oh no!” he thought. “I can’t get back!” He tried to pull himself out, but the blocks were too tight.

Elastic Band Dancer decided to try something. He saw a big red block and thought, “Maybe I can climb on top of it!” He started to grip with his flexible elastic. He moved slowly up and down, as if he were dancing. It was tiring! The blocks slipped a little under his fingers.

A little blue fluff ball, Leo, was watching him curiously. “Maybe you should try to make a circle!” Leo suggested. Elastic Band Dancer followed the advice and focused. With one last effort, he managed to wiggle free between the blocks!

Finally, with one last movement, he wriggled free between the blocks and went back to making spirals around his friend fluff ball Leo. He felt happy and a little tired, but also very proud of his ability to always find a solution. Every little step counts, and with a little ingenuity, you can overcome even the most difficult obstacles.

plan.problema: He had gotten stuck between the blocks and couldn’t get back!
plan.svolta: He decided to climb slowly up a big red block, gripping with his flexible elastic.
plan.finale: Finally, with one last effort, he squeezed between the blocks and returned to making spirals around his friend, the hair ribbon.

elastico per capelli.text:
Elastico Viola was in the playground. He was a bright purple rubber band, and he was just the right one! He loved to hold all the children’s hair. But today he wasn't happy. He felt loose and weak. He had lost all his colorful hair! It had fallen everywhere: on the green grass, on the golden sand, and even on a pair of red shoes.

Elastico Viola frowned. He was an important rubber band and he couldn’t afford to lose his colors. A little bird, Pipì, was watching him from a branch of a tree. “What’s wrong, Elastico Viola?” Pipì asked with his cheerful voice.

“I’ve come loose!” Elastico Viola replied sadly. “And I’ve lost all my hair!” He didn’t know what to do. Then he had an idea! He started to roll quickly around a big tree branch. He strained, he tightened, and he stretched. He felt strength growing inside of him.

Now he was stronger! And suddenly, the colorful hair started to reappear. One by one, they grabbed onto his purple body again. They were stronger than ever before. Pipì flew to a branch and sang: “Good job, Elastico Viola!”

Elastico Viola smiled. He was complete and happy again. He understood that with effort and strength, he could overcome any difficulty. And so, he continued to hold all the children’s hair in the playground.

plan.problema: He loosened up and lost all his colorful hair!
plan.svolta: He decided to roll quickly around a branch to gain strength.
plan.finale: The colorful hair started to cling to him, tighter than ever.

elastico per capelli.text:
Red Rubber lay on the playground grass. The sun shone brightly and the children were laughing around him. Red Rubber was a bright red hair elastic, but lately he had been feeling a little weak. He couldn't tie Sofia’s hair anymore, a little girl who loved to play there.

Sofia had long, blonde hair and every day Red Rubber let her make beautiful braids. But today something wasn't right. The elastic had come loose and its end was giving way. He couldn't hold Sofia’s hair together! He was frustrated, he felt like he was losing his purpose.

Red Rubber decided to do something. He quickly rolled around the stem of a yellow flower. He spun, spun, spun faster and faster. He felt a new strength, as if he was gaining energy from the sun and the earth. 

The movement made him feel stronger, more resilient. After a few turns, the elastic plunged vigorously towards Sofia’s hand. The girl took it, smiling. Carefully, Red Rubber tied Sofia’s hair into a perfect braid.

Sofia laughed with joy and hugged the red rubber. “Thank you, Red Rubber!” she said. Red Rubber felt happy. He had found his strength and his role.

plan.problema: He had loosened them and couldn’t hold a happy girl’s hair anymore.
plan.svolta: He decided to roll quickly around the stem of a flower to gain momentum and strength.
plan.finale: The girl smiled, taking the elastic and carefully tying her hair.

lollipop.text:
Lollipop was a very special candy. He was made of colorful sugar and had a little stick at the end. He lived in a row full of other lollipops, all just like him. They loved to look at each other and make bubbles with the wind.

One day, Lollipop found himself all alone. He was sitting on a park bench, but his colorful row was gone! He didn’t understand where his friends had gone. “Oh no!” thought Lollipop. “I’m lost!” He looked everywhere, but nothing. No other lollipop saw him.

Lollipop tried to shout: “Help! I’m lost!” But nobody heard him. He was too far from the noise of the children and the slides. So, Lollipop made a decision. He climbed off the bench with his stick holding him steady. He started to look among the swings, the water games, and the sandboxes.

While he wandered around the playground, he saw a little smiling gnome sitting on a stone. The gnome had a sweet smile and sparkling eyes. “What are you looking for, lollipop?” asked the gnome. Lollipop explained his situation with a shaky voice. The gnome listened carefully and then, after a while, he found Lollipop! He gently took him in his hands and slowly brought him back to his colorful row. All the lollipops were happy to see their lost friend again. 

Lollipop settled down next to his friends, grateful to be back home. The wait, even when it seemed long, helped Lollipop find his way.

plan.problema: Lollipop got lost from his row of colors and couldn’t find it.
plan.svolta: He tried to shout, but nobody could hear him, so he decided to get off the bench and look among the toys.
plan.finale: A little smiling gnome found Lollipop and calmly brought him back to his colorful row.
plan.morale: Patience is the key to solving problems.

lollipop.text:
Lollipop was a very special lollipop. He loved to play in the playground. He was made of colorful sugar and had a perfect stick to drag on the floor. One day, Lollipop was having fun rolling in the sand of the giant maze. He rolled, rolled, and… he found himself trapped!

The sand was high and soft around him. He couldn’t see his friend stick anymore. It was all gray and confusing. Lollipop was scared. He didn’t know how to get out of the sand maze. He felt lonely and a little sad.

Then, Lollipop had an idea! His bright red color shone in the sunlight. He decided to show it to everyone. He started to spin his stick hard, trying to get the attention of the children playing nearby. “Help!” he shouted with his squeaky voice. No one could hear him well among the laughter and the noise of the playground.

Then, a little girl stopped. She saw Lollipop shining in the maze. She smiled. “Look! A red lollipop!” she shouted loudly. Other children came closer, curious. Lollipop’s colorful smile hit them. They led him out of the sand maze.

Lollipop was happy! He was back at the playground and the children were very happy to have him back. He hugged his stick tight and he felt even more special. It was nice to help others, and this made him the happiest lollipop in the world. Kindness can solve problems.

plan.problema: The Lollipop got lost in the sand maze and couldn't find his way out.
plan.svolta: He decided to use his bright color to attract the children's attention and ask for help.
plan.finale: The children, struck by his colorful smile, led him out of the maze, very happy to have found him.

lollipop.text:
Lollipop was a giant lollipop, a lovely candy-pink color. He lived at the playground, among the swings and slides. He loved to watch the children playing, but he couldn’t play really. He was a special lollipop, a talking lollipop!

One day, Lollipop found himself all alone. He had gotten lost among so many colorful toys: blue balls, red cars, yellow building blocks. He couldn’t find his friends. “Oh no!” said Lollipop, “I’m lost!”

He tried to shout: “Hey! I’m here!”, but his voice was too small to be heard among all the playground noises. He called out to the blue ball, “Ball, Ball, where are you?” He shouted to the red car, “Car, Car, can you hear?” But nobody answered.

Lollipop was sad and a little scared. He felt small and invisible. Then, a ray of sunshine lit up his pink color. It was like a magic light that made him shine.

The other toys came closer, curious. The yellow ball, the green train, and the white doll gathered around Lollipop. They looked at him in amazement. “Wow! What a lovely color!” exclaimed the doll. 

Lollipop smiled. He was happy to see his friends again. He had shown that even if sometimes you feel lost, you should never give up looking. Because in the end, with a little patience and perseverance, you always find the solution.

plan.problema: Lollipop got lost among the many colors of the toys.
plan.svolta: He tried to call all his friends, but nobody could hear him.
plan.finale: Suddenly, a ray of sunshine illuminated his pink color, attracting the attention of the other toys who gathered around him.

lollipop.text:
Lollipop was a very happy lollipop. He lived at the playground and loved watching the children play. He was bright red, with a star-shaped tip. Lollipop always wanted to make new friends.

One day, Lollipop heard a lot of talking. “The gummy bear is missing!” shouted some children. The gummy bear was his best friend, a little yellow gummy bear. Lollipop was very worried. He hadn’t seen him for a while.

“Gummy bear? Gummy bear!” he called, but nobody answered. He was surrounded by so many colors: red, blue, green, yellow. Too many colors and too many people! Lollipop felt lost too.
